tagline: Delivering reliable energy, natural gas and water infrastructure to support sustainable growth in the Northeast
hero_kpi_rationale: Capex is the primary driver of regulated growth for Eversource, with $26.51 billion projected from 2026 to 2030, focused on electric and gas networks and resilience, positioning the company as a key player in critical infrastructure across New England.
company_description: Eversource Energy, a public utility holding company, engages in the energy delivery business. The company operates through Electric Distribution, Electric Transmission, Natural Gas Distribution, and Water Distribution segments. It is involved in the transmission and distribution of electricity; solar power facilities; and distribution of natural gas. The company also operates regulated water utilities that provides water services to residential, commercial, industrial, municipal and fire protection, and other customers in Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire. The company was formerly known as Northeast Utilities and changed its name to Eversource Energy in April 2015. Eversource Energy was incorporated in 1927 and is headquartered in Springfield, Massachusetts.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Amount invested annually in infrastructure such as electric and gas networks.
kpis.description: Investments in 2025 amount to $4.16 billion, down from $4.48 billion in 2024. A $26.51 billion plan is scheduled from 2026 to 2030.
kpis.signal: Capex declining in 2025 but planned at $26.51 billion from 2026 to 2030, demonstrating strong commitment to regulated infrastructure.

kpis.name: Operating cash flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated by the company's operating activities.
kpis.description: Operating cash flow reached $4.11 billion in 2025, compared to $2.16 billion in 2024.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement in operating cash flow from 2024 to 2025, reflecting stronger operational performance.

kpis.name: Earnings per share (non-GAAP)
kpis.explanation: Net income attributable to shareholders divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares outstanding, excluding exceptional items.
kpis.description: Non-GAAP earnings per share amounted to $4.76 in 2025, compared to $4.57 in 2024. Long-term EPS growth is projected between 5% and 7% from 2025 to 2030.
kpis.signal: Non-GAAP EPS growth reflects improved operational performance after excluding charges related to offshore wind and the sale of Aquarion.

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.explanation: Total amount of dividends paid per common share.
kpis.description: Dividends paid in 2025 amounted to $3.01 per share, compared to $2.86 per share in 2024. The quarterly dividend approved for 2026 is $0.7875 per share.
kpis.signal: Dividend increasing, reflecting management's confidence in stable cash flows and growth prospects.

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.788 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $1.101 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last three fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 65.0% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Regulated revenue base
kpis.explanation: Revenue growth from regulated segments (electricity, natural gas, water).
kpis.description: Eversource benefits from favorable regulatory decisions in 2025 (PSNH +$100.7M, Yankee Gas +$95.7M, NSTAR Gas rate reset), supporting regulated revenue growth.
kpis.signal: Growth driven by favorable regulatory outcomes and capital investments.

kpis.name: Infrastructure investment plan
kpis.explanation: Planned investment in critical infrastructure and network modernization.
kpis.description: Eversource projects a major investment plan including $1.23 billion for information technology and facility improvements, positioning the company for digital transformation and infrastructure resilience.
kpis.signal: Ambitious investment plan of $26.51 billion from 2026 to 2030, including $11.24 billion in electric distribution, $6.80 billion in natural gas, and $7.24 billion in electric transmission.

kpis.name: Dividend growth
kpis.explanation: Gradual increase in dividends paid to shareholders.
kpis.description: The quarterly dividend increased from $0.715 in 2024 to $0.7525 in 2025, and is approved at $0.7875 for 2026, reflecting steady growth aligned with EPS growth outlook.
kpis.signal: Increase in quarterly dividend to $0.7875 for 2026, reflecting confidence in cash flow generation and earnings sustainability.

kpis.name: Favorable regulatory framework
kpis.explanation: Positive impact of regulatory decisions on revenues and profitability.
kpis.description: State regulators (NHPUC, PURA, DPU) approved favorable rate increases and alternative regulatory frameworks, including the annual alternative regulatory framework for PSNH and the continuation of the PBR program for NSTAR Gas through 2030.
kpis.signal: Multiple favorable regulatory decisions in 2025 and 2026 support growth and improve visibility.

risks.title: AI-assisted cyberattacks
risks.summary: Cyberattacks are increasing in sophistication, magnitude, and frequency, targeting critical infrastructure. Geopolitical conflicts are accelerating this threat.
risks.score_rationale: The company is vulnerable to sophisticated cyberattacks involving AI, which could compromise critical electricity, gas, and water transmission and distribution systems. The potential impact on operations and reputation is significant.

risks.title: Regulation and allowed rates
risks.summary: State regulators (NHPUC, PURA, DPU) control tariffs, capital ratios, and allowed rates of return, determining profitability in regulated segments.
risks.score_rationale: Regulatory decisions directly impact revenues and profitability. Regulators may reject rate increases or impose stricter standards, affecting economic viability.

risks.title: Dependence on energy suppliers
risks.summary: Reliance on third-party suppliers creates risks related to the availability and cost of energy resources.
risks.score_rationale: The company depends on third-party suppliers for natural gas and energy. Factors such as inflation, supply tariffs, and geopolitical conflicts can affect costs.

risks.title: Operational reliability and performance
risks.summary: Reputation relies on the reliability and quality of electricity, gas, and water services. Public criticism and operational failures can impact financial results.
risks.score_rationale: Service reliability is essential. System failures, outages, or service interruptions can damage reputation and lead to regulatory penalties.

risks.title: Environmental compliance and energy transition
risks.summary: Environmental regulations require substantial investments in decarbonization and network modernization.
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to increasingly stringent environmental regulations regarding greenhouse gas emissions and water quality. Compliance and energy transition costs can be significant.

risks.title: Geopolitical tensions and critical security
risks.summary: Global conflicts increase cyber threats against utilities and may impact costs and resource availability.
risks.score_rationale: Geopolitical conflicts increase the risk of cyberattacks against critical infrastructure and may affect supply costs through trade sanctions and supply chain disruptions.

risks.title: Aquarion sale and regulatory uncertainty
risks.summary: The status of the Aquarion sale remains uncertain following regulatory rejection and ongoing appeal, impacting strategic clarity and valuation.
risks.score_rationale: PURA initially rejected the Aquarion sale in November 2025. An appeal was approved in January 2026, with a decision expected in March 2026. This uncertainty affects strategy and cash flows.

ai_positioning.summary: Eversource identifies AI-assisted cyberattacks as a growing risk in its 10-K filing, but has not yet announced major public AI deployment initiatives in operations. The company acknowledges that cyber threats are increasing in sophistication, including AI, and plans to invest in information technology as part of its 2026-2030 investment plan.
evidence: Cyberattacks that seek to exploit potential vulnerabilities in the utility industry are increasing in sophistication including artificial intelligence
Plan to invest $1.23 billion in information technology and facilities upgrades and enhancements from 2026-2030
